argument first this morning in Case 25-417,

 Mr. Walker.

 MR. WALKER: Mr. Chief Justice, and
may it please the Court:
 The power to create damages remedies

Bivens, Davis, and Carlson departed from that
 principle, and this Court has spent the last 45
 years trying to set things straight.  It has
 repeatedly explained that Bivens claims are
 disfavored, that they strain the separation of
powers, and that they cannot proceed if there
is any reason to think that Congress might be
better suited to weigh the costs and benefits
of a damages remedy. The Court has rejected
Bivens claim after Bivens claim after Bivens
 claim.
 But the Ninth Circuit allowed a Bivens
 remedy here anyway.  The Court may conclude
